subject: Newbie's question on package status/ getting package/ constructing own RENJIN package

messages.author: c1de4801913ea6c8
messages.subject: Newbie's question on package status/ getting package/ constructing own RENJIN package
parts:
Dear all,

I am new to R and RENJIN, and need help on some basic questions.

1. On the RENJIN package website (http://packages.renjin.org/index.html)  I see some red/green dots under the Package column. Could you please help to explain the meaning of different colors?
2. I find that some packages (e.g. quantnod, RCpp) do not have Apache Maven source, then how can I plug these packages into my Java application?
3. If I have a self-developed R package, how can I transfer it into a RENJIN package for java use?

Please kindly provide some help for such a newbie. Thanks A lot.

Regards
Andy

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: Newbie's question on package status/ getting package/ constructing own RENJIN package
parts:
Hi Andy,

  1. first of all, the http://packages.renjin.org site is a little old, but it does represent what is currently available in our public repository. Below you will find a rough overview of what the color of the bullets and rows in the table mean.
  2. if a package cannot be built for Renjin, there will be no XML to add to your POM file.
  3. packaging code for Renjin works slightly different from GNU R. Start by reading http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/writing-renjin-extensions.html and see if that makes sense to you. If not, let us know!

Red or grey status bullet -> will not load in Renjin and therefore does not work (also: all rows with these bullets are white)
Blue status bullet & green row -> will load in Renjin and should also work without problems in Renjin
Blue status bullet & yellow row -> will load in Renjin, but some functionality may be missing

Regards,

Maarten-Jan
